rows.title: At least 248,000 private-sector workers filed for pandemic bonuses
rows.standfirst: Connecticut’s Premium Pay Program bonus payouts may be months away. And with only $30 million to give out, each could be well under $1,000.

rows.title: CT employee unions to seek arbitration over pandemic pay
rows.standfirst: SEBAC’s decision comes after periodic discussions over 10 months with Gov. Ned Lamont’s administration failed to yield an agreement.

rows.title: Report: Poor CT cities should get $76.5 million in state investments
rows.standfirst: A state panel tasked with revitalizing CT’s poor urban centers is recommending financing for dozens of development projects in 12 communities.

rows.title: CT child care workers will get $1,000 bonuses, Lamont announces
rows.standfirst: Legislators say they approved $70 million for ongoing raises for ‘long-term change,’ not for one-time payments to child care workers.

rows.title: Towns say CT must remain a partner in upgrading school air quality
rows.standfirst: CT is using federal ARPA funds to help towns pay for air quality improvements in their schools. But what happens when that money runs out?

rows.title: CT contracting watchdog close to adding investigative team
rows.standfirst: The State Contracting Standards Board hasn’t been fully staffed since it was founded after former Gov. John Rowland resigned.

rows.title: Lamont sends relief checks to thousands of working poor families
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont’s administration sent checks averaging $170 to thousands of CT families. The GOP called the move an election-year gimmick.

rows.title: CT’s rainy day fund is full. One legislator wonders if it’s enough.
rows.standfirst: Some say CT is hoarding money, but one legislator is asking if CT it should boost the rainy day fund even more, to 20% of spending.
